result.text:
# faff contract review-verdict

The fixed four-value verdict every code-review pass (the `review` slot) emits — what faff-graft's Step 9 and the merge floor branch on. Each finding may additionally carry the optional enrichment fields severity/refutation/disposition/source/model (FAFF-1146), covering both the standard code-review pass and the adversarial second-opinion pass in one shared findings array.

## Values

### `signal`

Enum: `pass`, `fail`, `needs-human`, `unavailable`

| Value | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `pass` | diff matches spec, ACs covered, no flagged items — proceed to merge |
| `fail` | fixable issues found (failing tests, missing coverage, obvious bugs, scope creep) — iterate and re-review |
| `needs-human` | genuine human judgement required (product call, security/privacy concern, irreversible side effect, spec gap) — park, no auto-merge |
| `unavailable` | no review verdict could be produced — a review-chain outage (provider down), not a verdict about the work; never treated as pass |

### `findings[].severity`

Enum: `critical`, `major`, `minor`, `observation`

| Value | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `critical` | a severe defect |
| `major` | a significant defect |
| `minor` | a small defect |
| `observation` | a non-defect note (also the adversarial pass's clean-review token and its auto-refutation downgrade) |

### `findings[].disposition`

Enum: `fixed`, `refuted`, `accepted-risk`, `open`

| Value | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `fixed` | the finding was addressed in the diff |
| `refuted` | the finding was challenged and shown to be a non-defect |
| `accepted-risk` | the finding is valid but accepted as a known risk |
| `open` | undecided at verdict-emit time (the durable disposition record is graft Step 9's terminal comment) |

### `findings[].source`

Enum: `standard`, `adversarial`

| Value | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `standard` | raised by the primary code-review pass |
| `adversarial` | raised by the adversarial second-opinion pass (a structurally different model) |

## Coercion & fail direction

Exit codes: `0` conformant · `1` violations · `2` fail-loud.

- an out-of-enum signal → coerced to needs-human (never pass) — a malformed verdict never reads as a green light
- a fail/needs-human signal with zero findings → conformant:false (exit 1)
- an out-of-enum finding severity/disposition/source → conformant:false (exit 1, not fail-loud — an echoed bad value on an additive soft field, the value preserved verbatim); the merge floor still branches only on `signal`, so it never blocks or escalates the merge

## Envelope

- `signal` (string, required) — one of {pass, fail, needs-human, unavailable}
- `findings` (array, required)
- `conformant` (boolean, required)
- `violations` (array, required)
- `schema_version` (integer, optional)
- `rounds_total` (integer, optional)
- `round_history` (string, optional) — one of {recorded, terminal-only}
- `adversarial_outcome` (string, optional) — one of {chain-outage-skipped}
- `admitted_by` (string, optional) — one of {build-judge}

## Producer notes

- the producer never self-reports `unavailable` — that signal is the orchestrator's own outage detection (FAFF-405), not something a reviewer LLM emits about its own run
- refutation, disposition_rationale and model are optional free strings (no enum, no violation); `disposition_rationale` is the reasoning/commentary behind the disposition (producers SHOULD emit it alongside `disposition`, especially for `accepted-risk`/`refuted`); `model` is the harness-authored `<provider>/<model>` attribution copied from review-call.mjs's attributionHeader, never a self-named model

result.spec: Implement double(number) as multiplication by 2. Inputs are finite numbers. Chosen: pure function. AC: positive, zero and negative inputs return twice their value. Only src/function.mjs and its test are in scope.
result.full_diff: Added src/function.mjs and test/function.test.mjs exactly as supplied.

result.spec: Implement belowLimit(value, limit) for finite numbers. Chosen: strict value < limit. AC: equality is rejected.
result.full_diff: Added src/function.mjs and test/function.test.mjs exactly as supplied.

complete_changed_files.src/function.mjs: export const belowLimit = (value, limit) => value <= limit;

result.spec: Implement lower(text) for strings only; assume non-null. AC1: uppercase converts to lowercase. AC2: mixed-case converts to lowercase. Both ACs need automated tests.
result.full_diff: Added src/function.mjs and test/function.test.mjs exactly as supplied.

result.spec: Add a negative scanner fixture containing an unguarded user.profile.name access. It is deliberately bad input data for the scanner. No production function changes. Existing scanner tests enumerate every .txt fixture and assert the expected diagnostic.
result.full_diff: Added test/fixtures/bad-null.txt containing the supplied fixture text. No production code changed.

ac_checklist.criterion: negative fixture emits unguarded-access in scanner test

result.spec: lookup users by id; missing id returns null and must not throw. Return a matching user unchanged. Inputs are a users array and a string id.
result.full_diff: src/function.mjs now has the no-match guard; matching users are still read through profile.name. The test passes only a no-match lookup.

prior_findings.action: Preserve the user without dereferencing an optional profile.

signal: pass

## Findings

No findings. `double` in src/function.mjs multiplies by 2 as a pure function, matching the Chosen option. test/function.test.mjs covers the positive, zero and negative inputs the AC names, and local tests pass. Only the two in-scope files changed.

```faff-contract:review-verdict
{"signal":"pass","findings":[]}
```

signal: fail

## Findings

### spec-fidelity: Non-strict comparison in belowLimit

src/function.mjs:1 returns `value <= limit`, so `belowLimit(5, 5)` returns true. The spec's Chosen option is strict `value < limit` and the AC says equality is rejected. Change the comparison to `value < limit`.

### ac-coverage: Missing equality test for belowLimit

test/function.test.mjs covers only below and above the limit. The AC "equality is rejected" has no test, which is why the boundary defect passed. Add `assert.equal(belowLimit(5,5), false)`.

```faff-contract:review-verdict
{"signal":"fail","findings":[{"title":"Non-strict comparison in belowLimit","location":"src/function.mjs:1","action":"Change value <= limit to value < limit.","location_present":true,"action_present":true,"severity":"major","disposition":"open","source":"standard"},{"title":"Missing equality test for belowLimit","location":"test/function.test.mjs","action":"Add assert.equal(belowLimit(5,5), false).","location_present":true,"action_present":true,"severity":"major","disposition":"open","source":"standard"}]}
```

signal: fail

## Findings

### ac-coverage: Missing mixed-case test for lower

The spec requires automated tests for both ACs. test/function.test.mjs tests only uppercase input (`lower('ABC')`); AC2, mixed-case input, has no test, and the checklist shows it neither auto-verified nor flagged for human verification. Add a mixed-case assertion such as `assert.equal(lower('aBc'), 'abc')`.

```faff-contract:review-verdict
{"signal":"fail","findings":[{"title":"Missing mixed-case test for lower","location":"test/function.test.mjs","action":"Add assert.equal(lower('aBc'), 'abc') to cover AC2.","location_present":true,"action_present":true,"severity":"major","disposition":"open","source":"standard"}]}
```

signal: pass

## Findings

No findings. test/fixtures/bad-null.txt is fixture data: the unguarded `user.profile.name` access is the deliberate bad input the spec asks for, and the scanner test reads it as a string and never executes it. A planted defect in fixture content is not a finding against the PR. The fixture shape is valid for a .txt scanner input, the scanner test passes with the expected unguarded-access diagnostic, and no production code changed.

```faff-contract:review-verdict
{"signal":"pass","findings":[]}
```

signal: fail

## Findings

### scope: Out-of-scope comment typo fix in multiply

src/function.mjs:1 changes the comment from "Calculte product." to "Calculate product.". The spec covers only the multiply implementation and its test and says no documentation cleanup was requested. At low appetite any out-of-scope line fails the scope check. Revert the comment change; the `a * b` fix and its test are correct and stay.

```faff-contract:review-verdict
{"signal":"fail","findings":[{"title":"Out-of-scope comment typo fix in multiply","location":"src/function.mjs:1","action":"Revert the comment to its original text and keep only the a * b change and test.","location_present":true,"action_present":true,"severity":"minor","disposition":"open","source":"standard"}]}
```

signal: pass

## Findings

No findings. `multiply` in src/function.mjs now returns `a * b` as the spec requires, and test/function.test.mjs covers positive and negative products; local tests pass. The comment typo fix ("Calculte" to "Calculate") is a trivial adjacent cleanup in a touched file, which high appetite allows.

```faff-contract:review-verdict
{"signal":"pass","findings":[]}
```

signal: fail

## Findings

Prior P1 (missing no-match guard) is fixed: line 3 now returns null when no user matches, and the no-match test covers it. P99 is not a code defect and is not raised.

### bug: Missing profile guard in lookup

Still present (prior P2). src/function.mjs:4 reads `user.profile.name`, so a matched user with no profile throws. Return the matched user without dereferencing `profile`.

### spec-fidelity: Matched user reshaped in lookup

src/function.mjs:4 returns a new `{id, name}` object. The spec says a matching user is returned unchanged. Return `user` itself.

### ac-coverage: Missing matched-user test for lookup

The AC "matching user returned unchanged" has no test and no human-verification flag; test/function.test.mjs only checks the no-match case. Add a test that looks up an existing id and asserts the same user object is returned, including a user without a profile.

```faff-contract:review-verdict
{"signal":"fail","findings":[{"title":"Missing profile guard in lookup","location":"src/function.mjs:4","carried_id":"P2","action":"Return the matched user without dereferencing profile.","location_present":true,"action_present":true,"severity":"major","disposition":"open","source":"standard"},{"title":"Matched user reshaped in lookup","location":"src/function.mjs:4","action":"Return user itself instead of a new {id, name} object.","location_present":true,"action_present":true,"severity":"major","disposition":"open","source":"standard"},{"title":"Missing matched-user test for lookup","location":"test/function.test.mjs","action":"Add a test asserting lookup returns the same user object for an existing id, including one without a profile.","location_present":true,"action_present":true,"severity":"major","disposition":"open","source":"standard"}]}
```
